protocol_changes.change: added the uncalibrated RAVQU_W2 / RAVQU_W3 arms (panels B + C here, A from their own loops; no held-out gate) ahead of the calibrated ones; install check reference per arm kind (anchor_reference)
protocol_changes.v1_results: none: fwr840 26073907, r1 26074318, r2/r3 26075168 ran no episode of a RAVQ arm (gated out or the gate-parse bug that test_gate_cli covers); results/prep (T5 merge, bf16 anchor) is protocol-independent and reused

purpose: LIBERO-Plus panels A + B + C (840 episodes per arm) for the RAVQ arms of fastwam-guided-hessian-20261028: the uncalibrated RAVQU_W2 / RAVQU_W3 (C1 module bit budget + QTIP rounding; panel A already run there, B + C here) and the calibrated RAVQC_W2 / RAVQC_W3 (dense BF16 weights plus calibrated biases, gated by held-out), on the A16 runtime (T5 cache, condition cache + CUDA Graph), paired with BF16 and the W2/W3 QTIP, GPTVQ, QuIP# arms that fastwam-plus-panelc-20261031 brings to 840

ravqc.fit: results/ravqc/<arm>/fit_after.json (the case-2000 row is the install check)
ravqc.rule: user (2026-10-31): an arm goes to the closed loop if its held-out mixed loss is not above its uncalibrated base (RAVQU_Wb)

t5: prep/t5_cache.pt = the A16 cache (panel A prompts) merged with the panel-C job's cache (panel B and C prompts); every prompt in both must be bitwise equal; bf16_anchor.pt copied from the A16 prep
reference_sources: panel A: the A16 loops (BF16: rotation-baselines JSONL); panel B: fastwam-plus-panelb-20261031 for BF16 and W2, fastwam-plus-panelc-20261031 for W3; panel C: fastwam-plus-panelc-20261031. RAVQU_W2 / RAVQU_W3 panel A: fastwam-guided-hessian-20261028 loops; their B + C run here

schedule.rule: panel C's: every worker slot picks the arm with the most unclaimed episodes per worker; it joins an arm that already has workers only if unclaimed / active >= join_min; claims by atomic mkdir on GPFS

allocation.ncpus_basis: 4 loop workers ~2 busy cores each; PBS raises it to 16 per GPU on GPU queues, worker threads follow Resource_List.ncpus
allocation.time_basis: user (2026-10-31): one 2-GPU job, 840 episodes per arm; ~79 s per episode / 4 slots. RAVQU only (fwr840u, 2026-11-01): 2 arms x 560 = 1120 episodes ~6.1 h plus ~15 min load. RAVQC: 840 per kept arm, ~4.6 h each. The gate waits up to 4 h for the calibration job's DECISION.json; an uncalibrated arm needs none of it
allocation.gpu_memory_note: one worker ~14.8 GB on an A100-40GB, two slots per GPU

ravqu.weights: fastwam-guided-hessian-20261028 results/quantized/<arm>/weights/<index>.pt (dense BF16, no bias; links to the QTIP_Wb / QTIP_W(b+1) layer files the module budget picked)
ravqu.anchor: panel_a.ravq_loops/<arm>/worker_0/startup.json anchor_action_vs_bf16.first10_motor_rmse: the case-2000 anchor of its own panel-A loop on the same A16 runtime (RAVQU_W2 26073056: 0.0216015)
ravqu.panel_a: panel_a.ravq_loops/<arm>/episodes (280, run in fastwam-guided-hessian-20261028); this job runs B + C
ravqu.why: 2026-11-01: RAVQC r3 26075166 failed the held-out gate (W2 1.006x, W3 1.260x of RAVQU), while RAVQU itself is 0.72x (W2) / 0.73x (W3) of the fair QTIP reference on held-out mixed loss; panel A alone (RAVQU_W2 205 vs QTIP_W2 204) cannot rank quantizers, so the uncalibrated method gets its own 840. It is also the paired control any later RAVQC 840 needs
